# Community IPPE Exam Prep

For the Top200/300 Drugs:

- Study/know well the Top 35 medications for community practice that are posted on CORE (in the Document Library).

For the Calculations:

- Focus on calculations that you would use when dispensing medications in community pharmacy practice. For example the following:

o Convert lbs to kg
o Calculate a dose from a dosing regimen

▪ How much of a product to dispense from a given dose/concentration
▪ How much of a given product to use when compounding a liquid medication

- Examples of the types of questions that you could see on the exam from the APPE Ready example questions/solutions to questions documents (posted in the Document Library in CORE) are #28-30, 38, 39, 50, and 51.

For Errors and Omissions:

- Be able to review:

o A prescription
o Drug labeling/package insert
o Prescription label
o Product(s) used to dispense medication

- Determine whether there are any errors in prescription verification, compounding, dispensing, or labeling
- You may find these resources helpful as you prepare for the exam:

o https://www.powerpak.com/course/print/120287
o https://www.computertalk.com/prescription-monitoring-programs-the-errors-and-omissions-problem/
o https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/p2pdispensingerrors-0110

Dihydropyridine CCBs (calcium channel blockers)

Inhibit Ca from entering "slow channels" or select voltage-sensitive areas of vascular smooth muscle & myocardium during depolarization, resulting in relaxation of coronary vascular smooth muscle & coronary vasodilation. Directly acts on vascular smooth muscle to produce peripheral arterial vasodilation & ↓ peripheral arterial vasodilation ↓ing peripheral vascular resistance & BP.

MORE effect on vasodilation, NO effect on myocardial contractility		Amlodipine

(Adalat CC, Procardia XL)		HTN:
Amlodipine 5-10mg/day
Felodipine 2.5-10mg/d
Nifedipine 30mg/d (up to 120mg/d with Procardia XL)

Stable angina:
Amlodipine
Nicardipine
Nifedipine

Variant angina:
Amlodipine
Nifedipine		Reduce dose in hepatic impairment

(Caution in cirrhosis patients)		Common:
-peripheral edema
-flushing
-dizziness
-headache
-pulmonary edema

Rare, but serious:
-hepatoxicity
-thrombocytopenia		Efficacy:
-BP
-↓ chest pain/ ↓ number of angina attacks
-↓ prophylactic NTG use to relieve chest pain

Safety:
-s/s of peripheral edema
-Vitals^: BP, HR
-Labs^: LFTs

Contraindications:
-Nifedipine- Cardiogenic shock, STEMI, concomitant use of CYP3A4/5 inducers

Pregnancy/Lactation:
-Pregnancy: limited data available

**exception: nifedipine okay to use
-Lactation: d/c

^Baseline and f/u		- CYP3A/5 inducers: INC CCB metabolism, DEC effectiveness = monitor/ (dose increase)

- CYP3A/5 inhibitors: DEC CCB metabolism, INC risk of toxicity = monitor/ (dose decrease)

-NSAIDs: DEC anti-hypertensive effect= avoid / monitor

-Tacrolimus: INC risk of tacrolimus toxicity= monitor

Amlodipine:
-INC simva conc = NTE simva 20mg/d if used together		Clinical Pearls:
-first line agent for HTN (amlo & felo)
-use lower starting doses in elderly, small, or frail patients, or when adding to other antihypertensives

Counseling:
-report s/s of peripheral edema, fatigue, or hypotension
-avoid alcohol
-avoid NSAID use, if possible
-may cause dizziness; be cautious with driving
